ratings_why.fun: Clear arc from Duel bodies that win turn 1-3 fights to a fed Champion that multiplies itself late; three builds that share pieces make every shop a real choice.
ratings_why.distinct: Building the board out of gaps (Proud, empty-slot pay) plays unlike any of today's tribes, though Duel itself is familiar Start of Combat removal.

verdict_why: Every tier does its job and nothing is broken as written; further passes would mostly reshuffle numbers the owner will balance anyway.

points.text: The Chronicler checks at Start of Turn, before you shop, so the fat unit you mean to cross out has to sit through a fight and stop Elder and Gottfried paying. Making it End of Turn, or counting your hand, would make the Last Knight rhythm the build text describes actually work.

Refectory Prior is a Tier 2 card that does nothing until Tier 3, which is a dead buy on the turns Tier 2 economy matters most. A small payout before Tier 3 (1 gold at 3 or fewer units) would let it start the small-board line earlier.
The early game leans on Fir-Ridge Yearling alone for tempo; a second Duel body at Tier 2 would let the Duel line show up before Hartmut at Tier 3.

Herald with Ottokar means the Champion's first Duel is free, so a 3-gap board clears three front-row enemies before the fight. That is a fine late payoff; the UI should show those Duels so the fight doesn't feel decided off screen.

standouts.why: Squire Konrad is a perfect Tier 1 seed: grows in a corner, then cashes out into the Champion, so selling him is a decision.
Sir Gottfried is a capstone you build the whole board around, and his price (an empty board) is visible to every opponent.
Scarlet-Brow Marshal makes the chequerboard pay every turn and gives the Proud line its mid-game spine.

weakest.why: Refectory Prior is blank on Tier 2 turns.
Pennon-Squire's stats are still thin; its value is the keyword, which only matters in the Duel build.
Fantail Warden spends a Proud slot on one Shield, which a neutral can often do.

flags.note: x4 in fight (x7 golden) on a Champion already fed by Elder, Chronicler and Reisig is the tribe's runaway ceiling; the risk list already names a fallback rate.
With Master of the Cork-Pop, Sir Hartmut can chain up to four re-Duels and Sir Altmark's trophies double; worth a sim for pre-fight wipes.
Sir Altmark feeds the Champion from enemy size, so in late lobbies with huge boards the Champion grows fastest exactly when it is already biggest.
